haiku-low.q1: A pending login only: no session and no sid cookie. It sets the p2f cookie and sends the user to the code page.
haiku-low.q2: Only after setup is confirmed by a valid code. Sign-in ignores an unconfirmed secret until then.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code's hash must match an unused code, which is then marked used, and the session starts. An email reports the code use and remaining codes. Sign-in does not depend on that email; failed sends retry in the background.
haiku-low.q4: Expiry 5 minutes after the password check, or 5 wrong entries, deletes the pending login. The user returns to the password step.
haiku-low.q5: All of the user's other sessions are signed out. The current session stays.
haiku-low.q6: No. Once a time step is accepted, its code is refused again. Codes are accepted from the step before or after the current 30-second step.
haiku-low.q7: Turns 2FA on (or replaces the secret), records the time step, creates 10 new recovery codes shown once, deletes earlier recovery codes, and signs out other sessions. Partial-failure behaviour: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: In the pending_logins table as a token hash; the browser holds the random token in the p2f cookie. Removed on success, expiry at 5 minutes, or 5 wrong entries.
haiku-low.q9: user_totp holds the encrypted secret, confirmation status and last accepted time step; recovery_codes holds hashes. The exact rule for deciding 2FA is on: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: The current secret still protects sign-in until the new one is confirmed. An abandoned unconfirmed new secret is ignored; its cleanup or expiry: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: How the server tells the two code types apart: NOT STATED. Wrong recovery codes do count, since any wrong code adds 1 to the wrong-entry count.
haiku-low.q12: Not designed. The plan leaves this open: product must decide whether support may reset 2FA and how identity would be checked.

sonnet.q1: A pending login (expires in 5 minutes) and a p2f cookie. No session and no sid cookie.
sonnet.q2: Once the user types a valid code from the app and it is confirmed. Until then sign-in ignores the unconfirmed secret (for a replacement, the old secret keeps working).
sonnet.q3: The pending login is deleted, the p2f cookie cleared, start_session() runs, and enqueue_email() tells the user a code was used and how many unused codes remain. Sign-in does not depend on the email; failed sends are retried in the background.
sonnet.q4: The 5-minute expiry (or a missing pending login) or 5 wrong entries. The pending login is deleted and the user is sent back to the password step.
sonnet.q5: Every other session of that user is signed out. The current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. A time step already accepted for the user is refused. Drift tolerance is one 30-second step before or after the server's current step.
sonnet.q7: Four changes: 2FA turned on and time step recorded; 10 new recovery codes created (hashes stored, shown once); all earlier recovery codes deleted; all other sessions signed out. What happens if the update fails partway: NOT STATED.
sonnet.q8: In the pending_logins table (hashed token, user, wrong-entry count, expiry). The browser holds the random token in the p2f cookie. It is removed on successful sign-in, on 5 wrong entries, or when found missing or expired at code entry.
sonnet.q9: user_totp holds the encrypted secret (sealed with seal()), the confirmed flag and the last accepted time step (replay protection); recovery_codes holds hashed codes with used time. How '2FA on' is determined: NOT STATED explicitly; the document only says user_totp records whether setup is confirmed and that sign-in ignores an unconfirmed secret.
sonnet.q10: The current (old) secret still works for sign-in until the new one is confirmed. Abandoning: NOT STATED (whether an unconfirmed replacement expires is an open question).
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how the server distinguishes them. Per the document, any wrong code adds 1 to the wrong-entry count (implying wrong recovery codes count), but the document does not separately address this.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Product has not decided (e.g. whether support may reset 2FA, how identity is checked); the plan does not design that path.
